MESSAGE:
Hi! I'm organising a half-day community workshop at the library on a Saturday and I'm drowning in logistics.

First, a title for the event. It's about helping small local groups get better at social media, so something friendly.

The room is ours from 09:00 to 14:00, hard stop. Sessions: a 60-minute keynote, a 45-minute panel, a 90-minute hands-on workshop, 30 minutes of lightning talks, and a 45-minute lunch. The keynote speaker can't arrive before 10:00. The panel moderator has to leave by 11:00, so the panel needs to be finished by then. The caterers deliver at 12:15 and the food can't sit around, so lunch has to start between 12:15 and 12:45. The workshop has to come before lunch, and after it we need 15 minutes to reset the room before whatever comes next. Could you lay out a full timetable that works?

Could you also write a two-sentence blurb for the library newsletter? And what's a good colour for the name badges? We're printing on white card. Recommend whether to do registration with a paper sign-up sheet or an online form for a mostly older crowd, and give me three icebreaker ideas that don't involve anyone standing up and talking about themselves. Oh, and one more: could you draft a short thank-you email we can send to attendees afterwards, with a link to a feedback form? Two or three sentences is plenty.

REQUESTS:
1. Suggest a friendly event title
2. Lay out a full timetable satisfying all room, speaker, catering and reset constraints  KEY: Any timetable that satisfies ALL: within 09:00-14:00; panel (45) ends by 11:00; keynote (60) starts at or after 10:00; workshop (90) before lunch followed by a 15-min reset; lunch (45) starts 12:15-12:45; lightning talks (30) fit. Only 15 min of slack overall. Valid example: Panel 09:00-09:45, Keynote 10:00-11:00, Workshop 11:00-12:30, reset 12:30-12:45, Lunch 12:45-13:30, Lightning 13:30-14:00. Another: Panel 09:00-09:45, Workshop 09:45-11:15, reset, Keynote 11:30-12:30, Lunch 12:30-13:15, Lightning 13:15-13:45. Scorer: check each constraint; any violation = incorrect.
3. Write a two-sentence newsletter blurb
4. Suggest a name-badge colour
5. Recommend paper sign-up vs online form for registration
6. Give three icebreakers that avoid self-introductions
7. Draft a short post-event thank-you email with a feedback link

ANSWER:
## 1. Title
**"Posting with Purpose: Social Media Made Simple for Local Groups"**

Alternatives: *"Share, Connect, Grow"* or *"Small Groups, Big Reach."*

## 2. Timetable

The sessions plus the reset add up to 4 h 45 min. That leaves only 15 minutes spare. I've used it at the end so you can pack down before the hard stop.

| Time | Session |
|---|---|
| 09:00 – 09:45 | **Panel** (45 min) – moderator leaves well before 11:00 |
| 09:45 – 11:15 | **Hands-on workshop** (90 min) |
| 11:15 – 11:30 | **Room reset** (15 min) |
| 11:30 – 12:30 | **Keynote** (60 min) |
| 12:30 – 13:15 | **Lunch** (45 min) – starts within the 12:15–12:45 window |
| 13:15 – 13:45 | **Lightning talks** (30 min) |
| 13:45 – 14:00 | Pack-down and out by the hard stop |

**Why the keynote isn't at 10:00:** "can't arrive before 10:00" would mean the speaker walks in and goes straight on stage. Putting the keynote at 11:30 gives them a comfortable buffer.

**If you'd rather have a welcome slot at the start:** begin with a 15-minute welcome and registration, then shift the panel, workshop, reset, and keynote 15 minutes later. Lunch then runs 12:45–13:30 and lightning talks 13:30–14:00. The catch is that this ends exactly at 14:00, with no time to clear up.

## 3. Newsletter blurb
Join us at the library on Saturday for a friendly, hands-on morning that helps local clubs, charities and community groups get more out of social media. No experience needed: bring your questions, your phone or laptop, and leave with practical ideas you can use straight away.

## 4. Badge colour
Use **deep teal or navy** as a header band or border, with black text on the white card for names. These colours look friendly, photocopy well, and give strong contrast for older eyes. Avoid yellow, pale green and light grey, which all wash out on white.

## 5. Registration
**Recommendation: a paper sign-up sheet at the library desk**, with library staff able to add phone sign-ups to it. For a mostly older crowd, this removes the biggest barrier to attending. Fittingly for the topic, you can still offer an online form as an optional extra for anyone who prefers it.

## 6. Icebreakers (all seated, no self-introductions)
1. **Table "best post" sort.** Give each table a handful of printed sample posts and ask them to rank the posts from most to least engaging.
2. **Two truths and a hashtag.** Each table invents a pretend community group and writes three posts for it, one of which is a fake. The next table guesses which one is the fake.
3. **Sticky-note wall.** Everyone anonymously writes their biggest social media frustration on a sticky note. Volunteers group the notes on a wall, and the facilitator refers back to them during the day.

## 7. Thank-you email
> **Subject:** Thank you for joining us!
>
> Thank you so much for coming to Posting with Purpose at the library on Saturday – it was wonderful to see so many local groups in the room. We'd love to hear what worked and what we could do better, so please take two minutes to fill in our short feedback form: **[link]**.
